stories.headline: Introducing: Disclosure Season 2
stories.what_happened: Disclosure, the podcast dedicated to revealing the government’s inner workings, is back for Season 2 in audio and video. By law, nearly every move federal agencies make—every email, every memo, every receipt—belongs to the public. The key to gaining access is the Freedom of Information Act. In theory, FOIA obligates the government to open its files. But it also allows the government to hold back certain details, meaning that forcing transparency often requires a fight. Join Bloomberg investigative reporter Jason Leopold and First Amendment attorney Matt Topic for a guided tour of explosive details, bureaucratic foibles and details that govern

stories.headline: Parents of kids who need complex medical care at home tend to resolve frequent safety issues on their own, study finds
stories.what_happened: Approximately 1 in 20 U.S. children younger than 18 years of age are medically complex, meaning they have multiorgan system conditions like cerebral palsy and depend on implanted tube-related medical technology. These children receive most of their care at home, with parents responsible for handling complicated devices and managing intricate medication and nutrition regimens. In doing so, parents commonly encounter safety challenges, and they tend to come up with creative solutions without the care team's involvement, according to a study from Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago published in the journal Pediatrics.
